title: Product-key factorized Mirror code composition
hypothesis: A Cartesian product of two compact Mirror subcodes represents held-out compositions with lower actual bytes than flat independent function codes while preserving quality and distinct functions.
physical_object: shared 8x8 base operator and two banks of eight 8x8 basis operators
mirror_coordinate: pair (m1,m2), each selecting one of eight functional directions
logical_multiplicity: 64 composed operators, each evaluated for quality and distinctness
controls: Product-Key factorized address plus flat value table
direct two-coefficient code over same shared basis

development.selection_metric: held-out nMSE, collisions, distinct functions, actual bytes, lookup MAC proxy

storage.authority: actual deterministic ZIP/NPY inference payload after reload

success_gate: Both dev seeds: held-out nMSE <=1e-4; 64 distinct functions; Mirror >=10% smaller than flat and Product-Key; lookup MAC no higher than Product-Key; direct coefficient control >=10% larger for Mirror-specific value.
failure_gate: Any held-out nMSE >1e-3, fewer than 64 distinct functions, storage margin <10%, direct control within 10%, or lookup/runtime proxy >1.1x Product Key; fresh sealed.
boundaries: logical combination count is not capacity
